newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan prime minister wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan prime minister wins confidence vote.

text.p: Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif won a massive vote of confidence in the 217-seat National Assembly (lower house) on Wednesday and then vowed to move fast to implement a reform programme.
Assembly Speaker Ilahi Bakhsh Soomro said 181 members, out of 200 sworn in so far, had voted in favour of Sharif, who has yet to announce the composition of his cabinet.
The house elected Sharif prime minister on Monday by 177 votes to 16. Wednesday's confidence vote was a constitutional formality required within 60 days of his election.
"We will use this mandate in the interest of the nation," Sharif declared in a brief speech after the vote, whose result was greeted with applause from the house.
"We want to move forward fast," he said. "The condition of our cities and the condition of our villages must be improved. Law and order is in bad shape, it must be corrected."
Sharif was sworn in by President Farooq Leghari on Monday for a five-year term after leading his conservative Pakistan Muslim League party to a landslide victory in the February 3 general election.
The election followed Leghari's dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Bhutto, whose Pakistan People's Party (PPP) was routed at the polls, stayed away from Wednesday's assembly session.
Some other PPP deputies walked out before the confidence vote after the speaker disallowed a procedural objection raised by former PPP finance minister Naveed Qamar.
Sharif said his government would seek to implement his party's manifesto in a spirit of national consensus.
Noting that Pakistan had gained a reputation for rampant corruption, Sharif said: "Now is the time to make Pakistan number one in honesty."
Political sources said earlier that Sharif had drawn up a final list of cabinet members, but some decisions remained to be taken on allocation of portfolios.
Sharif's cabinet is expected to be much smaller than previous ones, which sometimes contained more than 30 ministers.
A caretaker government under Meraj Khalid stepped down on Monday.
